Paleolithic: Prehistoric period, first part of the Stone Age.
A former army general who once chaired NATO's Military Committee, this politician became the Czech Republic's fourth president in 2023 — who is he?
Petr Pavel: President of the Czech Republic since 2023. Born in Planá to a military family, Pavel enlisted right after graduating from military academy in 1983.
Denied a military commission in France by Louis XIV himself, this commander went on to serve the Habsburgs for six decades, becoming one of the greatest generals of his era — who was he?
Prince Eugene of Savoy: Military commander in the service of Austria (1663–1736)
He became Britain's first Labour prime minister in 1924, then was expelled from his own party in 1931 for leading a Conservative-dominated National Government — who was he?
Ramsay MacDonald: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (1924; 1929–1935)
The first person to navigate the Northwest Passage by sea, this Norwegian explorer later led the first party to reach the South Pole aboard the ship Fram — who is he?
Wounded five times in the Civil War — most seriously at South Mountain — this staunch abolitionist and brevet major general went on to become the 19th president; who was he?
Rutherford B. Hayes: President of the United States from 1877 to 1881.
Renowned in the Book of Genesis for her hospitality and beauty, this matriarch was the wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac — who is she?
Sarah: Biblical matriarch. Sarah (originally Sarai) is a biblical matriarch, prophet, and major figure in Abrahamic religions.
In the Book of Revelation, these divine horn blasts — sounded one at a time by angels after the breaking of the final seal — unleash a series of apocalyptic disasters. What are they called?
Seven trumpets: Described in the Book of Revelation. The seven trumpets are sounded by seven angels and the events that follow are described in detail in Revelation 8–11.
Originating from an Old English word meaning 'being truly guilty,' this concept covers immoral or wrongful thoughts, words, or acts across many religions — what is it?
A former Mathematical Economics professor at IIT Delhi known for Hindu nationalist views, he led the Janata Party until 2013 before joining the BJP — who is this Indian politician?
Subramanian Swamy: Indian politician. Subramanian Swamy (born 15 September 1939) is an Indian politician, economist and statistician.
A Princeton and Harvard Law graduate who became the first Hispanic American to represent the Lone Star State in the Senate, he led the charge in the 2013 government shutdown — who is he?
Ted Cruz: American politician and attorney (born 1970)
A former financial-services man who started on the Charleston County Council, he became the first African-American senator from the South to be directly elected — which South Carolina Republican?
Tim Scott: American politician and businessman (born 1965)
In 2023, 1.3 million applicants competed for just 1,255 government job openings through this Indian constitutional body's exams — what is it?
Union Public Service Commission: India's central recruiting agency.
The youngest presidential candidate in the 2024 Republican primaries, this Harvard and MIT graduate founded a biotech company and is now seeking the Ohio governorship. Who is he?
Vivek Ramaswamy: American entrepreneur and politician (born 1985)

Controlling most of Eastern Galicia from late 1918 to mid-1919, this short-lived state also claimed parts of northern Bukovina and Carpathian Ruthenia, with power held by a nationalist democratic party — what was it called?
West Ukrainian People's Republic: 1918–1919 state in Central Europe.
This man is the younger brother of China's current top leader, and serves as president of an international energy conservation and environmental protection association — who is he?
Xi Yuanping: Son of Xi Zhongxun, brother of Xi Jinping.
China's premier through the 1980s, he was the architect of political reform — until his support for the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests cost him all his power. Who is this fallen reformer?
Which of these four was born earliest?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Mikhail Lomonosov (born 1711) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?

Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four. Originally specified in the late 1950s, it is the second-oldest high-level programming language still in common use, after Fortran.
Which of these was founded earliest?
MUMPS (founded 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Donna Strickland is a physicist. Donna Theo Strickland (born May 27, 1959) is a Canadian optical physicist and pioneer in the field of pulsed lasers.
Who among these is a chemist?
Stephanie Kwolek is a chemist. Stephanie Louise Kwolek (July 31, 1923 – June 18, 2014) was a Polish-American chemist known for inventing Kevlar (poly-paraphenylene terephthalamide).
What is the atomic number of Moscovium?
Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
What is the atomic number of Bismuth?
Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
In what year was Harold Shipman born?
Harold Shipman: Harold Frederick Shipman (14 January 1946 – 13 January 2004) was an English doctor in general practice and serial killer.
In what year was Fritz Haber born?
Fritz Haber: For this work, Haber has been called one of the most important scientists and industrial chemists in human history.
In what year was Ludwig Wittgenstein born?
Ludwig Wittgenstein: Wittgenstein was born in Vienna into one of Europe's richest families.
In what year did Lewis Carroll die?
Lewis Carroll: An avid puzzler, Carroll created the word ladder puzzle, which he called "Doublets", which was published in Vanity Fair magazine between 1879 and 1881.
In what year did Max Weber die?
Max Weber: Born in Erfurt in 1864, Weber studied law and history in Berlin, Göttingen, and Heidelberg.
In what year was Potassium discovered?
Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K (from Neo-Latin kalium) and atomic number 19.
SEPECAT Jaguar: Breguet Aviation. As of 2026, the Jaguar remains in service with only the Indian Air Force.
Which country is Sukhoi Su-17 from?
Sukhoi Su-17: Soviet Union. The Sukhoi Su-17 (Russian: Су-17; NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
Who is credited with discovering Pavo?
Pavo (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Pavo is a constellation in the southern sky whose name is Latin for 'peacock'.
Who is credited with discovering Nitroglycerin?
Nitroglycerin: Ascanio Sobrero. It is combined with nitrocellulose to form double-based smokeless powder, used as a propellant in artillery and firearms since the 1880s.
Who is credited with discovering Lithium?
Lithium: Johan August Arfwedson. Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

The only living member of its entire taxonomic order, this nocturnal African mammal digs into termite and ant hills using sharp claws and powerful legs — related distantly to elephants and manatees, what is it?
Aardvark (Orycteropus afer) is a medium-sized, burrowing, nocturnal mammal native to Africa.
Sometimes called emotional blindness, this neuropsychological condition involves trouble identifying or describing one's own feelings, and appears in about half of autistic people. What is it?
Alexithymia (-), also called emotional blindness, is a neuropsychological phenomenon characterized by difficulties processing or describing one's emotions.
This joint region where the foot meets the leg comprises three joints built from the talus, tibia, and fibula, enabling the foot's up-and-down flexing motions — what body part is it?
Ankle is the area where the foot and the leg meet.
Four novels and fifty-six short stories about a certain consulting detective made his name — but this knighted British writer-physician also invented Professor Challenger. Who was he?
Arthur Conan Doyle (22 May 1859 - 7 July 1930) was a British writer and physician.
Not contagious and believed to be partly genetic, this multi-system inflammatory condition can also cause blood clots, aneurysms, or blindness in severe cases — which condition?
Behçet's disease (BD; sometimes written Behcet) is a type of inflammatory disorder which affects multiple parts of the body.
The third-most-produced bomber in history, this American four-engine heavy bomber dominated the European Theater and dropped more bombs than any other plane in WWII — which aircraft is it?
Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress is an American four-engined heavy bomber aircraft that was developed in the mid-1930s for the United States Army Air Corps (USAAC).

Synthesized by the liver in response to inflammation, this ring-shaped blood molecule binds to the surface of dead or dying cells to activate the immune system's complement cascade. What is it commonly called?
C-reactive protein (CRP) is an annular (ring-shaped) pentameric protein found in blood plasma, whose circulating concentration rises in response to inflammation.
Portuguese explorers carried this tropical American tree to India in the 16th century; today Ivory Coast and India lead a 3.9-million-ton global harvest of its nut — what is it?
Cashew is the common name of a tropical evergreen tree Anacardium occidentale, in the family Anacardiaceae.
Born in 1847, this American wore three hats at once — psychologist, logician, and mathematician. Who was she?
Christine Ladd-Franklin (December 1, 1847 - March 5, 1930) was an American psychologist, logician, and mathematician.
This activity involves designing algorithms and writing code in high-level languages so a machine can follow step-by-step instructions to perform tasks. What is it?
Computer programming is the composition of sequences of instructions, called programs, that computers can follow to perform tasks.

This closed sac within the body has a distinct wall of cells that are structurally abnormal compared to surrounding tissue, and may contain air, fluid, or semi-solid material — unlike a pus-filled abscess, what is it called?
Cyst is a closed sac in the body, having a distinct envelope and division compared with the nearby tissue.
Bred around 1890 in Thuringia by a tax collector seeking a loyal protector, this German working-dog breed is known in North America by a slightly different two-word name — which breed?
Dobermann is a German breed of medium-large working dog of pinscher type.
Many of these Northern Hemisphere shade trees, prized along old European and American streets, were wiped out by a fungus carried by bark beetles — which tree genus is this?
Elm are deciduous and semi-deciduous trees comprising the genus Ulmus in the family Ulmaceae.
Distinct from secretion, this bodily process includes exhaling carbon dioxide, sweating, and passing urine through the bladder and urethra — what's it called?
Excretion is elimination of metabolic waste, which is an essential process in all organisms.
This American physician-scientist discovered genes tied to several diseases, led the Human Genome Project, and went on to direct the NIH under three presidents — who is he?
Francis Collins (born April 14, 1950) is an American physician-scientist who discovered the genes associated with a number of diseases and led the Human Genome Project.
This flowering plant genus, whose name derives from the Latin word for a small sword, belongs to the iris family and is centered on the Cape Floristic Region of South Africa — which genus?
Gladiolus (from Latin, the diminutive of gladius, a sword) is a genus of perennial cormous flowering plants in the iris family (Iridaceae).
This perception occurs with no external stimulus at all, yet feels completely real to the person experiencing it — distinct from dreaming, illusions, or ordinary imagination — name this phenomenon?
Hallucination is a perception in the absence of an external context stimulus that has the compelling sense of reality.
The largest of the eusocial wasps, some species in this genus can exceed 50 millimetres in length. What insect is it?
Hornet are wasps of the genus Vespa in the subfamily Vespinae (the vespine wasps).

Native to South China and Vietnam, this evergreen tree produces a star-shaped fruit whose spice tastes like anise, and whose oil a drugmaker relied on until switching to genetically modified E. coli in 2012 — name this tree?
Illicium verum (star anise or badian, Chinese star anise, star anise seed, star aniseed and star of anise) is a medium-sized evergreen tree native to South China and northeast Vietnam.

Designed under the philosophy 'write once, run anywhere,' this high-level, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language compiles to bytecode executed by a dedicated virtual machine — name the language?
Java (programming language) is a high-level, general-purpose, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language.
Diagnosed via corneal topography and linked to frequent eye rubbing and allergies, this progressive disorder causes the cornea to bulge into a cone shape — which eye condition?
Keratoconus is an eye disorder in which the cornea, the transparent front part of the eye, gradually thins and bulges outward into a cone shape.
Its pale golden coat is patterned not with simple dots but with dark spots clustered into rings called rosettes, and it has prowled Africa and Asia since the Early Pleistocene — which big cat is it?
Leopard (Panthera pardus) is one of the five extant cat species in the genus Panthera.
Named for their strong, monogamous pair bonding and the long stretches paired birds spend sitting together, this small genus of African parrots is popular as a pet — what is it commonly called?
Lovebird is the common name for the genus Agapornis, a small group of parrots in the Old World parrot family Psittaculidae.
Covering everything from B2B deals to a government's 'Got Milk?'-style campaigns, this business pillar means acquiring, satisfying and retaining customers — what is this discipline called?
Marketing is the act of acquiring, satisfying and retaining customers. It is one of the primary components of business management and commerce.
What neurological disorder causes moderate-to-severe, often one-sided headaches, frequently accompanied by nausea, light and sound sensitivity, and sometimes preceded by a sensory 'aura'?
Migraine is a neurological disorder that causes moderate-to-severe headaches. The pain usually affects one side of the head.
With shells that are elongated and wedge-shaped rather than round, these bivalves attach themselves to shorelines using threads nicknamed a "beard" — what are they?
Mussel is the common name used for members of several families of bivalve molluscs, from saltwater and freshwater habitats.
A reddish-brown gas that's a key step in making nitric acid for fertilizer, it also seeps into homes from gas-stove cooking and harms indoor air — which compound, formula NO2?
Nitrogen dioxide is a chemical compound with the formula NO2.
This systemic skeletal disorder develops when the rate of bone breakdown outpaces new bone formation with age, leaving bones porous, less dense, and prone to fracture — what's the condition called?
Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disorder characterized by low bone mass, micro-architectural deterioration of bone tissue leading to more porous bone, and consequent increase in fracture risk.

This psychiatric disorder describes an adult's primary or exclusive sexual attraction to children who haven't yet reached puberty, with diagnostic criteria extending the age cutoff to 13 — what is it called?
Pedophilia (alternatively spelled paedophilia) is a psychiatric disorder in which an adult or older adolescent experiences a primary or exclusive sexual attraction to prepubescent children.
This French physicist shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with his wife, making them the first married couple ever to win a Nobel — who is he?
Pierre Curie (15 May 1859 - 19 April 1906) was a French physicist and chemist, and a pioneer in crystallography and magnetism.
A purplish-black salt that dissolves into an intensely pink-to-purple solution, this strong oxidizer doubles as a WHO-listed medicine for cleaning wounds and dermatitis — what is it?
Potassium permanganate is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula KMnO4.
A polyphenol from the flavonoid family with a naturally bitter taste, this compound turns up in capers and red onions and gets added to supplements — what is it?
Quercetin is a plant flavonol from the flavonoid group of polyphenols.

Winner of the 1905 Nobel Prize for his work on tuberculosis, this German physician identified the causative agents of tuberculosis, cholera, and anthrax, earning him the nickname 'father of microbiology' alongside Louis Pasteur — name this scientist?
Robert Koch (KOKH; 11 December 1843 - 27 May 1910) was a German physician and microbiologist.
This systematic discipline builds testable explanations about nature and society, and is continuously challenged and validated by the community that practices it. What is it?
Science is a systematic discipline that builds and organises knowledge in the form of testable explanations about nature and society.
Long, thin and transparent, this hydrozoan drifts through the ocean as a colony of specialized zooids that together handle feeding, floating and jet propulsion — what marine organism is this?
Siphonophore (from Ancient Greek (siphn), meaning "tube" and - (-phros), meaning "bearing") are cnidarian animals of the hydrozoan order Siphonophorae.
Haunted by the Holocaust and the Eichmann trial, this American social psychologist ran his notorious obedience experiments in a Yale basement in 1961. Who was he?
Stanley Milgram (August 15, 1933 - December 20, 1984) was an American social psychologist who conducted controversial experiments on obedience in the 1960s during his professorship at Yale.
Deriving its name from a French word for crushed oak bark used in hide-curing, this class of astringent plant compounds binds to and precipitates proteins and other organic molecules — what is it?
Tannin (or tannoids) are a class of astringent, polyphenolic biomolecules that bind to and precipitate proteins and various other organic compounds including amino acids and alkaloids.
Shaped like a butterfly and located in the neck just below the Adam's apple, this endocrine gland's two lobes are joined by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus — name the gland?

Thyroid is an endocrine gland in vertebrates. The lower two thirds of the lobes are connected by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus (pl.: isthmi). The thyroid gland secretes three hormones: the two thyroid hormones – triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4) – and a peptide hormone, calcitonin.
This break in the skin or mucous membrane involves tissue breakdown severe enough to expose the dermis or fat beneath, and often becomes infected with pus — what condition is it?
Ulcer (dermatology) is a sore on the skin or a mucous membrane, accompanied by the disintegration of tissue.
This slender, short-legged predator's genus also includes polecats, stoats, and ferrets, and its smallest species is the tiniest carnivore on Earth — what animal is it?
Weasel are mammals of the genus Mustela of the family Mustelidae.
Earning his doctorate in Islamic philosophy at George Washington University under Seyyed Hossein Nasr, this Turkish academic now directs the country's National Intelligence Organization — who is he?
İbrahim Kalın (born 15 September 1971) is a Turkish bureaucrat and academic who is the current director of the National Intelligence Organization (MT).
Considered sacred by Hindus and Buddhists, this tree native to the Indian subcontinent is also known as bael and is the sole member of its genus — which species?
Aegle marmelos: Species of tree, considered sacred by Hindus. It is present in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Nepal as a naturalized species.

An anatomist and archaeologist turned TV presenter, she has served as professor of Public Engagement in Science at the University of Birmingham since 2012 and once led the charity Humanists UK — who is she?
Alice Roberts: English academic, TV presenter and author.
Nominated by Donald Trump in 2020, this Notre Dame law professor became the fifth woman to serve as a US Supreme Court associate justice after previously sitting on the Seventh Circuit — who is she?

Amy Coney Barrett: US Supreme Court justice since 2020. Barrett graduated from Rhodes College before attending Notre Dame Law School, earning a Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree in 1997 and ranked first in her class.
Who is this — “American-Yemeni Islamic cleric and lecturer (1971–2011)”?
Anwar al-Awlaki: American-Yemeni Islamic cleric and lecturer (1971–2011). Al-Awlaki was the first U.S. citizen to be targeted and assassinated by a U.S. government drone strike.

Also known by a folksy nickname, this small North American tree produces a custard-textured fruit tasting like banana or pineapple — despite containing a neurotoxin elsewhere in the plant. What species is it?
Asimina triloba: Species of tree. Asimina triloba, the American papaw, pawpaw, paw paw, or paw-paw, among many regional names, is a species of small deciduous tree.
This fig tree spreads outward indefinitely by growing extra trunks from its own prop roots, and its most famous species is the national tree of India — what is it?
Both heads of this upper-arm muscle originate on the scapula and let you flex your elbow while turning your palm upward — what muscle is it?

Biceps: Muscle on the front of the upper arm. While the long head of the biceps crosses both the shoulder and elbow joints, its main function is at the elbow where it flexes and supinates the forearm.

Flying for the U.S. Air Force since 1955, this subsonic strategic bomber evolved from a six-turboprop straight-wing design into eight swept-wing turbojets and can haul up to 70,000 pounds of weapons — what's its name?
Boeing B-52 Stratofortress: American strategic bomber aircraft.

This Italian-American physicist invented an improved coincidence circuit and traveled to Eritrea to prove cosmic rays arrive more strongly from the West than the East, before Italy's racial laws forced him to flee — who was he?
Which multidrug-resistant fungal yeast colonizes skin in long-term care facilities and causes bloodstream infections with up to a 60% mortality rate?
Also known by the nickname 'catawba,' this genus of flowering trees is native to warm regions of North America, the Caribbean, and East Asia — what genus is it?
Native to the mountains of Honduras and Guatemala and nicknamed the 'custard apple' for its creamy texture, this fruit was called 'the most delicious fruit known to men' by Mark Twain — which fruit?
Cherimoya: Edible fruit-bearing species of plant.
What is this — “Physiological phenomenon involving the engorgement of the clitoris”?

Clitoral erection: Physiological phenomenon involving the engorgement of the clitoris. Clitoral erection (also known as clitoral tumescence or female erection) is a physiological phenomenon where the clitoris becomes enlarged and firm.
One of the most intensively studied and intelligent cephalopods, this mollusk ranges from the Mediterranean and English coastline all the way to South Africa — which species?
Common octopus: Species of cephalopod. The common octopus (Octopus vulgaris) is a mollusk belonging to the class Cephalopoda.
These feather-gilled freshwater crustaceans share their taxonomic order with lobsters and turn up in everything from brooks to rice paddies — what are they?
Crayfish: Freshwater crustaceans. Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans belonging to the infraorder Astacidea, which also contains lobsters.
The first Western European combat aircraft to break Mach 2 in level flight, achieving the feat in October 1958, which French fighter jet family was this?
Dassault Mirage III: French supersonic fighter/interceptor aircraft.

Discovered in Arizona in the 1940s and first classified as a species of Megalosaurus, this theropod was reassigned to a new genus in 1970 once paleontologists noticed the twin crests on its skull — which dinosaur?
Dilophosaurus: Genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic.

Coined by Robert Spitzer in the late 1970s to replace the notion of a "depressive personality," this condition resembles major depression but lingers for at least two years — and now goes by "persistent depressive disorder." What was its original name?
Dysthymia: Psychiatric disorder defined by chronic depression.
Caused by viruses like herpes simplex or rabies, this inflammation of the brain can bring fever, confusion, and a stiff neck — what is this condition?

Encephalitis: Inflammation of the brain. The severity can be variable with symptoms including reduction or alteration in consciousness, aphasia, headache, fever, confusion, a stiff neck, and vomiting.
This complex-analysis identity states that e raised to the power of ix equals cosine x plus i times sine x, linking exponential and trigonometric functions — what is it called?
Euler's formula: Complex exponential in terms of sine and cosine. The formula is still valid if x is a complex number, and is also called Euler's formula in this more general case.
Its 41 living species boast the most varied fur patterns of any land carnivore, all armed with retractile claws and an obligate taste for meat — which family is this?
Felidae: Family of mammals. Felidae ( FEE-lə-dee) is the family of mammals in the order Carnivora colloquially referred to as cats.

First described by 19th-century French psychiatrists Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, this rare condition — also called shared psychotic disorder — lets one person's delusion spread to another. What is it called?

Folie à deux: Shared psychosis, a psychotic disorder. The disorder, first conceptualized in 19th century French psychiatry by Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, is also known as Lasègue–Falret syndrome.
Sometimes called 'poor man's pepper' or 'pepper grass,' this fast-growing herb has a peppery bite similar to mustard — which plant?
Garden cress: Species of edible herb.

This general term covers any organ that secretes substances either straight into the bloodstream, like endocrine ones, or through a duct to a body surface, like exocrine ones — what type of structure is it?
Gland: Type of animal organ. A gland may also function to remove unwanted substances such as urine from the body.
Known to the British as the Martlet, this American carrier-based fighter entered service in 1940 and remained the U.S. Navy's best fighter against the Mitsubishi Zero until mid-1943 — which aircraft?
Grumman F4F Wildcat: United States Navy World War II era fighter plane.
This German physicist was the first to conclusively demonstrate the electromagnetic waves predicted by James Clerk Maxwell's equations — who is he?
Introduced in 1948 by a French naturalist, this taxonomic tribe groups humans together with chimpanzees and bonobos, but excludes gorillas — which tribe?
Hominini: Tribe of mammals. The Hominini (hominins) form a taxonomic tribe of the subfamily Homininae (hominines).

Responsible for nearly half a million deaths each year, this condition occurs when the body produces or absorbs more heat than it can dissipate, most often from heat stroke or a drug reaction — what condition?
Hyperthermia: Elevated body temperature due to failed thermoregulation.
This concept in calculus, a continuous analog of a sum, computes the signed area under a curve and pairs with differentiation as one of the field's two fundamental operations?
This fragrant genus of shrubs and vines in the olive family is grown in vast quantities in one Egyptian village that supplies much of the world's perfume industry — which plant?
Jasmine: Genus of flowering plant in the olive family Oleaceae.
Born Giulia Maddalena Angela in Italy, this physician became a leading freethinker and activist for women's rights and social reform in early-20th-century Argentina — who is she?
Julieta Lanteri: Argentine doctor and activist (1873–1932)

Ranked alongside Aristotle and Frege among history's most significant logicians, this thinker proved his completeness theorem in his 1929 Vienna dissertation before publishing his famous incompleteness theorems two years later — who is he?
Kurt Gödel: Mathematical logician and philosopher.
Marked by weariness and a desire to act without the energy to do so, which condition can be a normal response to poor sleep or stress, or a sign of underlying illness?
Lethargy: State of tiredness, weariness, fatigue, or lack of energy.
Reaching about 200 kg at its largest, this reddish-brown-shelled reptile ranges through the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans as well as the Mediterranean — which species?
Loggerhead sea turtle: Species of marine reptile distributed throughout the world.
A former mayor of Tehran and engineer by training, he served as Iran's sixth president from 2005 to 2013 and championed the country's nuclear program — who is he?

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad: President of Iran from 2005 to 2013. Mahmoud Ahmadinejad (né Sabbaghian; born 28 October 1956) is an Iranian politician who served as the sixth president of Iran from 2005 to 2013.

Born from a US-UK cooperative effort begun in the early 1970s to improve on a first-generation jump jet, this vertical-takeoff-capable attack aircraft has served the US Marine Corps plus Spanish and Italian navies — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas AV-8B Harrier II: Anglo-American VSTOL ground-attack aircraft.
Sold under brand names like Ritalin and Concerta, which stimulant medication is preferred as the first-line treatment for ADHD in children, while amphetamine is favored for adults?
Nicknamed 'Viper Zero' and built with a 60/40 Japan-US manufacturing split, this fighter derived from the F-16 was the first combat aircraft to carry an AESA radar — what jet is it?
Mitsubishi F-2: Japanese supersonic jet fighter.
Which condition describes a total absence of speech that can result from injury, illness, trauma, or a developmental or neurological disorder — sometimes only temporary?
Muteness: Medical condition. In human development, muteness or mutism is defined as an absence of speech, with or without an ability to hear the speech of others.
This medical term for a birthmark or mole covers marks present at birth as well as ones that appear later in life — what is it called?
Nevus: Mole or birthmark; visible, circumscribed, chronic skin lesion.
Thriving in the cool, wet summers of Northwest Europe, this hardy cereal grass tolerates low-nutrient, acidic soil and is dominated globally by Canadian and Russian production?
Derived from an ancient Roman unit called the uncia, this measure comes in an avoirdupois version equal to 1/16 of a pound and a heavier troy version used for precious metals — what unit is it?
Ounce: Unit of mass. The ounce is any of several different units of mass, weight, or volume and is derived almost unchanged from the uncia, an Ancient Roman unit of measurement.
Also called androgenetic alopecia, this condition driven by male sex hormones and genetics shows up as a receding hairline or a thinning crown in men — what's the common name for it?
Pattern hair loss: Medical condition. Pattern hair loss, also known as androgenetic alopecia, is a hair loss condition that primarily affects the top and front of the scalp.
Native to Eurasia but now introduced worldwide, this game bird has been flagged in the UK as a threat to endangered native adders — what is it?

Commonly known as plantains or fleaworts — though unrelated to the banana-like cooking fruit of the same name — this genus of roughly 200 mostly herbaceous flowering plants tops out around 24 inches tall. Which genus?
Plantago: Genus of flowering plants. Plantago is a genus of about 200 species of flowering plants in the family Plantaginaceae, commonly called plantains or fleaworts.
This glucocorticoid medication used to suppress the immune system is actually a prodrug that the liver must convert into its active form before it works — what is it?
Prednisone: Steroid medication. It is also used to treat high blood calcium due to cancer and adrenal insufficiency along with other corticosteroids.
Often starting as a blood clot in the leg that travels to the lungs, this blockage can cause chest pain on breathing in, coughing up blood, and sudden death — what is the condition?

Pulmonary embolism: Blockage of an artery in the lungs. Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a blockage of an artery in the lungs by a substance that has moved from elsewhere in the body through the bloodstream (embolism).

Native to the eastern Himalayas and southwestern China, this small mammal sports dense reddish-brown fur, a ringed tail, and curved semi-retractile claws for climbing — and was the original bearer of its famous name. What is it?
Red panda: Species of mammal in Asia.
First created in 1994 near Darmstadt, Germany, this extremely radioactive synthetic element is named for the physicist who discovered X-rays — which element is it?
Roentgenium: Chemical element with atomic number 111 (Rg)
Also called elder or elderberry, this tree or shrub's flowers and berries are traditionally used to make cordial and wine — what's its scientific name?
Sambucus nigra: Species of flowering plant in the moschatel family.
When an infection-triggered immune overreaction sends blood pressure plummeting and disrupts cells throughout the body, doctors in the ICU are treating this life-threatening condition — what is it?
Septic shock: Dangerously low blood pressure due to damage from an organ infection.
Roughly 21 feet long yet coiled to fit inside the abdomen, this digestive tube receives bile and pancreatic juice and is divided into the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum — which organ?
Small intestine: Organ in the gastrointestinal tract.
Prized as the standard soundboard material for stringed instruments, this coniferous genus has four-sided needles and dominates boreal forests across the Northern Hemisphere — which tree genus?

Formed by a merger of two iconic American food giants and co-headquartered in Chicago and Pittsburgh, this company owns brands like Oscar Mayer, Philadelphia Cream Cheese, and Grey Poupon — which food conglomerate is it?

Kraft Heinz: American multinational food company. Kraft Heinz is the third-largest food and beverage company in North America and the fifth-largest in the world with over $26.0 billion in annual sales as of 2021.
